examples.target: 這件事佈滿社交媒體。

examples.source: Do not plaster stickers all over the desk.
examples.target: 不要把貼紙貼滿書桌。

examples.source: After missing lessons, he had to play catch-up.
examples.target: 缺課後，他要努力趕上。

examples.source: The company is playing catch-up with its rivals.
examples.target: 公司正努力追趕對手。

examples.source: Do not wait until the last week to play catch-up.
examples.target: 不要等到最後一週才追趕進度。

examples.source: The report played down the problem.
examples.target: 報告淡化了問題。

examples.source: He tried to play down his mistake.
examples.target: 他嘗試淡化自己的錯誤。

examples.source: Do not play down the importance of sleep.
examples.target: 不要貶低睡眠的重要性。

play fast and loose with.meaning: 隨便對待 / 不嚴格遵守

examples.source: The writer plays fast and loose with historical facts.
examples.target: 作者隨便對待歷史事實。

examples.source: Companies should not play fast and loose with safety rules.
examples.target: 公司不應隨便對待安全規則。

examples.source: The article criticises leaders who play fast and loose with promises.
examples.target: 文章批評不嚴格遵守承諾的領袖。

play for laughs.meaning: 以搞笑方式呈現 / 當作笑料

examples.source: The scene is played for laughs.
examples.target: 這一幕以搞笑方式呈現。

examples.source: The writer plays the mistake for laughs.
examples.target: 作者把錯誤當作笑料。

examples.source: Serious topics should not always be played for laughs.
examples.target: 嚴肅題材不應總是當作笑料。

play into someone's hands.meaning: 正中某人下懷 / 落入某人圈套

examples.source: Arguing in public played into his hands.
examples.target: 公開爭吵正中他下懷。

examples.source: Do not let anger play into your opponent's hands.
examples.target: 不要讓憤怒令你落入對手圈套。

examples.source: The careless reply played into the critic's hands.
examples.target: 粗心的回覆正中評論者下懷。

play out a role.meaning: 扮演某種角色 / 演出某種形象

examples.source: The actor played out the role of a strict teacher.
examples.target: 演員演出嚴格老師的形象。

examples.source: In the debate, she played out the role of a careful critic.
examples.target: 在辯論中，她扮演謹慎批評者的角色。

examples.source: The story lets children play out different roles.
examples.target: 故事讓孩子扮演不同角色。

play up to.meaning: 迎合 / 配合某人的期待

examples.source: The speaker played up to the crowd.
examples.target: 演講者迎合群眾。

examples.source: The advertisement plays up to parents' worries.
examples.target: 廣告迎合家長的憂慮。

examples.source: He played up to the image of a funny student.
examples.target: 他配合搞笑學生的形象。

examples.source: The idea plays well with younger students.
examples.target: 這個想法受較年輕學生歡迎。

examples.source: Simple examples play well with beginners.
examples.target: 簡單例子對初學者有效。

examples.source: The message did not play well with parents.
examples.target: 這個訊息不受家長歡迎。

play with time.meaning: 操控時間感 / 玩弄時間呈現

examples.source: The film plays with time through flashbacks.
examples.target: 電影透過倒敘操控時間感。

examples.source: The writer plays with time in the final chapter.
examples.target: 作者在最後一章玩弄時間呈現。

examples.source: Stories can play with time to create surprise.
examples.target: 故事可以操控時間感來製造驚喜。

examples.source: She pleaded with her parents to let her join.
examples.target: 她懇求父母讓她參加。

examples.source: The students pleaded with the teacher for more time.
examples.target: 學生央求老師給多些時間。

examples.source: He pleaded with his friend to tell the truth.
examples.target: 他懇求朋友說出真相。

examples.source: The mall hosted a pop-up immersive exhibition.
examples.target: 商場舉辦了一個快閃沉浸式展覽。

examples.source: Students visited a pop-up immersive art space.
examples.target: 學生參觀了一個快閃沉浸式藝術空間。

examples.source: The pop-up immersive show lasted only one week.
examples.target: 快閃沉浸式表演只持續一星期。

examples.source: She pored over the notes before the exam.
examples.target: 考試前她仔細查看筆記。

examples.source: The class pored over the poem line by line.
examples.target: 全班逐行鑽研那首詩。

examples.source: He pored over the map before the trip.
examples.target: 出發前他仔細查看地圖。

examples.source: The rule creates a possibility for abuse.
examples.target: 這條規則造成被濫用的可能性。

examples.source: The article warns of the possibility for abuse.
examples.target: 文章警告有被濫用的可能性。

examples.source: Clear checks can reduce the possibility for abuse.
examples.target: 清晰檢查可以減少被濫用的可能性。

examples.source: She poured everything into her final project.
examples.target: 她全力投入畢業項目。

examples.source: The team poured everything into the match.
examples.target: 隊伍全力投入比賽。

examples.source: He poured everything into helping his students.
examples.target: 他全力投入幫助學生。

preach to the converted.meaning: 向本來已同意的人宣講 / 多此一舉地說服同路人

examples.source: Telling teachers that reading matters is preaching to the converted.
examples.target: 跟老師說閱讀重要，是向本來已同意的人宣講。

examples.source: The speech only preached to the converted.
examples.target: 演說只是多此一舉地說服同路人。

examples.source: The campaign must reach new people, not preach to the converted.
examples.target: 宣傳必須接觸新人，而不是只向同路人宣講。

press one's advantage.meaning: 乘勝追擊 / 進一步利用優勢

examples.source: The team pressed its advantage after scoring.
examples.target: 隊伍入球後乘勝追擊。

examples.source: She pressed her advantage in the final round.
examples.target: 她在最後一輪進一步利用優勢。

examples.source: Good debaters know when to press their advantage.
examples.target: 好的辯論員知道何時乘勝追擊。

priced out.meaning: 因價格太高而買不起的

examples.source: Many young people feel priced out of the housing market.
examples.target: 很多年輕人覺得樓價太高而買不起樓。

examples.source: Students were priced out of the expensive course.
examples.target: 學生因課程太貴而負擔不起。

examples.source: Fans were priced out by the high ticket cost.
examples.target: 粉絲因票價太高而買不起。

priced out of the market.meaning: 因價格太高而被市場排除的

examples.source: Small buyers were priced out of the market.
examples.target: 小買家因價格太高而被市場排除。

examples.source: Rising rents priced families out of the market.
examples.target: 租金上升令家庭被市場排除。

examples.source: The article explains why students are priced out of the market.
examples.target: 文章解釋為何學生因價格太高而被市場排除。

primed for.meaning: 準備好迎接 / 有望出現

examples.source: The team is primed for success.
examples.target: 隊伍已準備好迎接成功。

examples.source: The market is primed for change.
examples.target: 市場有望出現改變。

examples.source: After months of practice, she is primed for the contest.
examples.target: 經過數月練習，她已準備好迎接比賽。

examples.source: Some companies profit off user data.
examples.target: 有些公司從用戶資料獲利。

examples.source: The article asks who profits off the new rule.
examples.target: 文章問誰從新規則獲利。

examples.source: It is wrong to profit off other people's hardship.
examples.target: 從別人的困難中獲利是不對的。

puff away.meaning: 不停吸煙 / 吞雲吐霧

examples.source: The old novel describes men puffing away outside the station.
examples.target: 舊小說描寫男人在車站外不停吸煙。

examples.source: The health article warns against puffing away every day.
examples.target: 健康文章警告不要每天吞雲吐霧。

examples.source: He stood by the door, puffing away in silence.
examples.target: 他站在門旁，沉默地不停吸煙。

examples.source: The fake advert tried to pull the wool over customers' eyes.
examples.target: 假廣告企圖蒙騙顧客。

examples.source: Do not let smooth words pull the wool over your eyes.
examples.target: 不要讓花言巧語蒙騙你。

examples.source: The article explains how scams pull the wool over people's eyes.
examples.target: 文章解釋騙案如何蒙騙人。

pull to shreds.meaning: 嚴厲批評 / 批得體無完膚

examples.source: The reviewer pulled the film to shreds.
examples.target: 評論者把電影批得體無完膚。

examples.source: Classmates should not pull each other's work to shreds.
examples.target: 同學不應把彼此的作品批得體無完膚。

examples.source: The proposal was pulled to shreds in the meeting.
examples.target: 建議在會議中被嚴厲批評。

examples.source: The headline puns on the word light.
examples.target: 標題用 light 這個字作雙關語。

examples.source: The advert puns on the product name.
examples.target: 廣告用產品名稱作雙關語。

examples.source: Writers often pun on words with two meanings.
examples.target: 作家常用有兩個意思的字作雙關語。

punch above one's weight.meaning: 表現超出自身規模 / 以小搏大

examples.source: The small school punches above its weight in debate.
examples.target: 這間小學校在辯論方面表現超出自身規模。

examples.source: Hong Kong often punches above its weight in finance.
examples.target: 香港在金融方面常以小搏大。

examples.source: The team punched above its weight and reached the final.
examples.target: 隊伍表現超出自身規模，打入決賽。

examples.source: Teachers should guide students, not push beliefs down their throats.
examples.target: 老師應引導學生，而不是把信念強加於人。

examples.source: The writer dislikes campaigns that push beliefs down people's throats.
examples.target: 作者不喜歡把信念強加於人的宣傳。

examples.source: Good discussion does not push beliefs down someone's throat.
examples.target: 好的討論不會把信念強加於人。

push into the limelight.meaning: 推到聚光燈下 / 使受到關注

examples.source: The award pushed the young writer into the limelight.
examples.target: 獎項把年輕作家推到聚光燈下。

examples.source: The news pushed the issue into the limelight.
examples.target: 新聞使這個議題受到關注。

examples.source: Social media can push ordinary people into the limelight.
examples.target: 社交媒體可以把普通人推到聚光燈下。

push past one's fears.meaning: 克服恐懼 / 越過恐懼

examples.source: She pushed past her fears and spoke on stage.
examples.target: 她克服恐懼，上台發言。

examples.source: Students need support to push past their fears.
examples.target: 學生需要支持去克服恐懼。

examples.source: He pushed past his fears and joined the contest.
examples.target: 他越過恐懼，參加比賽。

push someone's buttons.meaning: 刺激某人反應 / 觸動某人情緒

examples.source: That comment really pushed her buttons.
examples.target: 那句話真的觸動了她的情緒。

examples.source: He knows how to push his brother's buttons.
examples.target: 他知道怎樣刺激弟弟反應。

examples.source: Do not push someone's buttons just to win an argument.
examples.target: 不要為了贏爭論而故意刺激別人。

examples.source: The rule puts a ceiling on ticket prices.
examples.target: 規則為票價設下上限。

examples.source: Do not put a ceiling on students' dreams.
examples.target: 不要限制學生的夢想。

examples.source: The policy puts a ceiling on rent increases.
examples.target: 政策限制租金加幅。

examples.source: The mistake put a dent in his confidence.
examples.target: 這個錯誤削弱了他的信心。

examples.source: High prices put a dent in family budgets.
examples.target: 高物價損害家庭預算。

examples.source: The win put a dent in their rival's hopes.
examples.target: 這場勝利削弱了對手的希望。

examples.source: The photo helped me put a name to a face.
examples.target: 照片幫我把樣貌和名字對上。

examples.source: At the meeting, I finally put a name to a face.
examples.target: 在會議上，我終於把樣貌和名字對上。

examples.source: A class list helps new teachers put names to faces.
examples.target: 班名單幫新老師把樣貌和名字對上。

put a positive spin on.meaning: 正面包裝 / 說成好事

examples.source: The spokesperson put a positive spin on the delay.
examples.target: 發言人把延誤正面包裝。

examples.source: She tried to put a positive spin on the bad news.
examples.target: 她嘗試把壞消息說成好事。

examples.source: The article puts a positive spin on failure.
examples.target: 文章把失敗正面包裝。

put a spring in one's step.meaning: 令某人精神一振 / 令某人步伐輕快

examples.source: The good news put a spring in her step.
examples.target: 好消息令她精神一振。

examples.source: A short walk can put a spring in your step.
examples.target: 短途散步可以令你精神一振。

examples.source: Winning the prize put a spring in his step.
examples.target: 得獎令他步伐輕快。

put bums on seats.meaning: 吸引觀眾入場 / 賣座

examples.source: Famous actors put bums on seats.
examples.target: 著名演員能吸引觀眾入場。

examples.source: The festival needs events that put bums on seats.
examples.target: 節日需要賣座的活動。

examples.source: A catchy title can help put bums on seats.
examples.target: 吸引人的標題可以幫助吸引觀眾入場。

examples.source: In the historical novel, the prisoner was put in irons.
examples.target: 在歷史小說中，囚犯被戴上鐵鐐。

examples.source: The phrase put in irons appears in old prison stories.
examples.target: put in irons 這個片語出現在舊式監獄故事中。

examples.source: The captain ordered the rebel to be put in irons.
examples.target: 船長下令把叛亂者囚禁起來。

put in the hard yards.meaning: 付出艱苦努力 / 刻苦訓練

examples.source: She put in the hard yards before the final.
examples.target: 決賽前她付出艱苦努力。

examples.source: Good writers put in the hard yards by revising.
examples.target: 好的作家透過修改付出艱苦努力。

examples.source: The team put in the hard yards during training.
examples.target: 隊伍在訓練中刻苦訓練。

examples.source: The principal put the new plan into motion.
examples.target: 校長啟動新計劃。

examples.source: One email put the whole project into motion.
examples.target: 一封電郵使整個項目開始。

examples.source: The meeting put several changes into motion.
examples.target: 會議啟動了幾項改變。

put my foot down.meaning: 堅決反對 / 下定決心制止

examples.source: I had to put my foot down about the noise.
examples.target: 我不得不堅決反對噪音問題。

examples.source: The teacher put her foot down when students cheated.
examples.target: 學生作弊時，老師下定決心制止。

examples.source: He put his foot down and refused the unfair rule.
examples.target: 他堅決反對，拒絕不公平規則。

put my name on.meaning: 以自己名義保證 / 署名支持

examples.source: I would not put my name on a careless report.
examples.target: 我不會以自己名義保證一份粗心的報告。

examples.source: She put her name on the petition.
examples.target: 她署名支持請願。

examples.source: The author proudly put his name on the book.
examples.target: 作者自豪地在書上署名。

put on offer.meaning: 推出發售 / 放出拍賣

examples.source: The shop put the new bags on offer.
examples.target: 商店推出新袋發售。

examples.source: The painting was put on offer at an auction.
examples.target: 那幅畫被放出拍賣。

examples.source: Tickets were put on offer online first.
examples.target: 門票先在網上推出發售。

put one's hand up.meaning: 主動請纓 / 自願參與

examples.source: She put her hand up to lead the group.
examples.target: 她主動請纓帶領小組。

examples.source: Few students put their hands up for the task.
examples.target: 很少學生自願參與任務。

examples.source: He put his hand up when the team needed help.
examples.target: 隊伍需要幫忙時，他主動請纓。

put one's head above the parapet.meaning: 冒險出頭 / 公開表態承受批評

examples.source: She put her head above the parapet and criticised the rule.
examples.target: 她冒險出頭，批評規則。

examples.source: Few leaders put their heads above the parapet on this issue.
examples.target: 很少領袖在這議題上公開表態承受批評。

examples.source: Writers sometimes put their heads above the parapet.
examples.target: 作家有時會冒險出頭。

put one's money where one's mouth is.meaning: 用實際行動支持自己所說的話

examples.source: If you support the project, put your money where your mouth is.
examples.target: 如果你支持項目，就用實際行動支持自己所說的話。

examples.source: The company put its money where its mouth was and funded scholarships.
examples.target: 公司用實際行動支持承諾，資助獎學金。

examples.source: He put his money where his mouth was by volunteering every week.
examples.target: 他每週做義工，用實際行動支持自己所說的話。

put one's name to.meaning: 公開支持 / 掛名支持

examples.source: She put her name to the campaign.
examples.target: 她公開支持這個運動。

examples.source: The scientist refused to put his name to weak research.
examples.target: 科學家拒絕掛名支持薄弱研究。

examples.source: Many teachers put their names to the letter.
examples.target: 很多老師在信上署名支持。

put one's needs ahead of.meaning: 把某人的需要放在...之前

examples.source: Good leaders do not put their needs ahead of the team.
examples.target: 好領袖不會把自己的需要放在團隊之前。

examples.source: Parents often put children's needs ahead of their own.
examples.target: 父母常把孩子的需要放在自己之前。

examples.source: The article asks if companies put profit ahead of workers' needs.
examples.target: 文章問公司是否把利潤放在員工需要之前。

put out of one's misery.meaning: 結束痛苦 / 使不再受苦

examples.source: The teacher put us out of our misery and gave the answer.
examples.target: 老師給出答案，終於結束我們的焦急等待。

examples.source: Just tell me the result and put me out of my misery.
examples.target: 直接告訴我結果，讓我不用再焦急吧。

examples.source: The final clue put the class out of its misery.
examples.target: 最後的提示使全班不用再苦苦猜想。

put out of reach.meaning: 令...難以負擔 / 令...不能取得

examples.source: High prices put the course out of reach for many families.
examples.target: 高價令很多家庭難以負擔這課程。

examples.source: The shelf put the books out of reach of small children.
examples.target: 書架令小孩不能取得那些書。

examples.source: Rising rents put city homes out of reach.
examples.target: 租金上升令市區住宅難以負擔。

examples.source: The rain put paid to our picnic plans.
examples.target: 大雨使我們的野餐計劃落空。

examples.source: The injury put paid to his hopes of winning.
examples.target: 受傷終結了他獲勝的希望。

examples.source: The new evidence put paid to the rumour.
examples.target: 新證據終結了謠言。

examples.source: Her hard work put everyone to shame.
examples.target: 她的努力令所有人自愧不如。

examples.source: The young player put older players to shame.
examples.target: 年輕球員令較年長球員自愧不如。

examples.source: His neat notes put mine to shame.
examples.target: 他整齊的筆記令我的筆記自愧不如。

examples.source: Who put you up to this prank?
examples.target: 是誰唆使你做這個惡作劇？

examples.source: The story suggests his friend put him up to it.
examples.target: 故事暗示是他的朋友唆使他做的。

examples.source: Do not let others put you up to breaking rules.
examples.target: 不要讓別人唆使你違反規則。

examples.source: The message put my mind at rest.
examples.target: 這個訊息使我放心。

examples.source: The doctor put her mind at rest with a clear explanation.
examples.target: 醫生清楚解釋，使她放心。

examples.source: A quick phone call put his parents' minds at rest.
examples.target: 一個簡短電話使他的父母放心。

put something into perspective.meaning: 使某事更易理解 / 讓人看清情況

examples.source: The chart puts the problem into perspective.
examples.target: 圖表使問題更易理解。

examples.source: Talking to her put my worries into perspective.
examples.target: 跟她談話讓我看清自己的憂慮。

examples.source: History can put today's changes into perspective.
examples.target: 歷史可以讓人看清今日的改變。

put something on the back burner.meaning: 暫時擱置某事 / 把某事放到次要位置

examples.source: We put the project on the back burner during exams.
examples.target: 考試期間，我們暫時擱置項目。

examples.source: The school put the idea on the back burner.
examples.target: 學校把這個想法放到次要位置。

examples.source: Do not put your health on the back burner.
examples.target: 不要把健康放到次要位置。

put the cash in the tills.meaning: 帶來實際銷售 / 令店舖有收入

examples.source: Popular snacks put the cash in the tills.
examples.target: 受歡迎的小食為店舖帶來實際銷售。

examples.source: The festival put the cash in the tills for local shops.
examples.target: 節日令本地店舖有收入。

examples.source: Good marketing can put the cash in the tills.
examples.target: 好的市場推廣可以帶來實際銷售。

put the finishing touches to.meaning: 作最後修飾 / 完成最後工序

examples.source: She put the finishing touches to her poster.
examples.target: 她為海報作最後修飾。

examples.source: The team put the finishing touches to the presentation.
examples.target: 隊伍完成簡報的最後工序。

examples.source: He put the finishing touches to the model before class.
examples.target: 上課前，他為模型作最後修飾。

put too much weight on.meaning: 過分重視 / 過分倚重

examples.source: Do not put too much weight on one test result.
examples.target: 不要過分重視一次測驗結果。

examples.source: The article puts too much weight on exam scores.
examples.target: 文章過分倚重考試分數。

examples.source: Parents may put too much weight on rankings.
examples.target: 家長可能過分重視排名。

putter around.meaning: 慢慢行駛 / 悠閒地移動

examples.source: The old boat puttered around the harbour.
examples.target: 舊船在海港慢慢行駛。

examples.source: He puttered around the garden on Sunday.
examples.target: 他星期日在花園悠閒地走動。

examples.source: Small cars puttered around the village streets.
examples.target: 小車在村路上慢慢行駛。
